clue.text: Was red as could be leaving the beach

indicators.note: 'as could be' suggests the letters might be something else, so the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sunburnt as red as possible heads away from the sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges WAS RED AS; the 'as' of 'as could be' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving off the shore takes you toward open water, the direction this adverb describes.

clue.text: Inadequate, throwing many into a panic

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a scare is a panic or alarm
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: A thin supply sends crowds into a frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in short supply is insufficient, not enough.

clue.text: The man's not given a rise in any situation

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
in a down clue a rise means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

explanation.surface: Someone is refused a pay rise whatever the circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a rise' turns NOT into TON, which goes in ANY. The man is Mark Antony, Roman general; 'The man's' reads as 'the man is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Antony is the Roman figure whose name is given, a specific male name.

clue.text: A journalist holding public transport is exploited

parts.note: a bus is public transport
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A reporter on a bus is being taken advantage of.
explanation.definitionFit: To be misused or taken advantage of is to be exploited.

clue.text: Withdraws papers said to be controversial

indicators.note: controversial suggests the letters are disputed and stirred into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone pulls out after newspapers report a contentious remark.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish or go away from view is to withdraw.

clue.text: Alarms and anxiety aboard ship

indicators.note: something aboard a vessel sits within it, so one piece goes inside the ship's letters

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
care means worry or anxiety

explanation.surface: Panic and worry spread among those on a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean frightens or startles someone, as verbs.

clue.text: Winsome child preparing for a fight

parts.note: arming is getting weapons ready for battle

explanation.surface: A sweet youngster gears up for a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone attractively pleasing.

clue.text: One of the guns returned-had a meal to order

indicators.note: returned means the gun's name is read backwards

parts.note: a Luger is a German pistol
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: After a gun was handed back, someone ate to order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses LUGER into REGUL; the dash and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To control or keep in proper order is to regulate.

clue.text: Repeatedly produce notes needed by a prison

indicators.note: repeatedly says the word is used twice in a row

parts.note: to sing is to produce musical notes

explanation.surface: Inmates sing over and over in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Sing Sing is a famous maximum-security prison in New York State.
explanation.definitionFit: Sing Sing is a well-known New York penitentiary.

clue.text: The French back new unit-trust that's humanitarian

indicators.note: back tells us to read the French article from right to left

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the

indicators.note: new signals the letters of unit and trust are made fresh in a different order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit

explanation.surface: A French firm promotes a fresh investment fund with a charitable aim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LA into AL; 'new' mixes I (one, a unit) with TRUST to give TRUIST. 'unit-trust' looks like one financial product but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A person devoted to the welfare of others is a benefactor of humankind, a humanitarian.

clue.text: To adulterate alcoholic drink gives an edge

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or adulterate
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Watering down the spirits gives a dealer a profit edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is the border or edge of a page or area.

clue.text: Scorn but study allure

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
to tempt is to entice or allure

explanation.surface: A student is caught between disdain and attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean disdain felt for something judged worthless.

clue.text: Markets about a thousand scents

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped round the other

parts.note: to market goods is to sell them
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A trader sells about a thousand perfumes at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: To scent something is to detect it by the nose, to sniff it.

clue.text: A means of securing clean linen

definitions.text: A means of securing clean linen

parts.words: A means of securing clean linen
parts.note: a small wooden or plastic clip that holds washing to the line

explanation.surface: How to keep fresh sheets safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip pins laundered washing to a line while it dries.

clue.text: A military commander should be quite impervious

definitions.meaning: the Duke who beat Napoleon at Waterloo
a rubber boot named after that Duke, which ought to keep water out

explanation.surface: A general ought to be unmoved by anything.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Duke led British forces at Waterloo, and the waterproof rubber boot bears his title.

clue.text: Convince people coins used are counterfeit

parts.note: P stands for pence, British coins

indicators.note: counterfeit means fake, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Talk people into believing the money they spent was fake.
explanation.definitionFit: To persuade someone is to talk them into belief.

clue.text: Identified the youth pocketing a peach

indicators.note: pocketing means putting inside, so one piece is held by the other

parts.note: a lad is a youth
a peach is an attractive person, a belle

explanation.surface: A young man was spotted stuffing a fruit in his pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagged or categorised means named, identified.

clue.text: He's above all mundane things

parts.note: read literally: one who travels high above the earth, beyond worldly matters

explanation.surface: A lofty man disdains the everyday.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut journeys far above the earth.

clue.text: Taxes a peer may well find cause great irritation

indicators.note: may well suggests the letters could well turn up in another order

explanation.surface: A lord facing tax bills will be thoroughly annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: To infuriate someone is to irritate them intensely.

clue.text: Start putting points to a solicitor

parts.note: SE is southeast, combining two compass points
a tout solicits custom, so is one who solicits

explanation.surface: A lawyer gets the first instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin a journey or task is to set off.

clue.text: 20 A trial could result in the noose!

indicators.note: could result in suggests the letters might turn into something new

explanation.surface: A court case might end in a hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's rope with a running loop is a lasso.

clue.text: There's a series of races — aim to be there

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A race calendar gives spectators a reason to come.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend is to be present at an event.

clue.text: Drawing small boat

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A picture of a little yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough drawing is a quick outline picture.

clue.text: Soldiers authorised hold the front in question

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: hold means contain, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: let means allowed or authorised
van, short for vanguard, is the front of an army

explanation.surface: Troops cleared to hold the front line face an inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pertinent bears directly on the matter being discussed.

clue.text: The coolness of a quiet trainee with incomplete bomb

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

indicators.note: incomplete means the word bomb loses a letter, here its first

explanation.surface: A calm learner handles an unfinished explosive device.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-assurance under pressure is composure, the coolness of the unflustered.

clue.text: Facing work, attitudinise about it

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word it goes inside

parts.note: to pose is to strike an attitude

explanation.surface: Confronting a job, a poser strikes attitudes around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposite means across from, directly facing.

clue.text: The conclusion is not all attend in good faith

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, so the letters lie within them

explanation.surface: The finale comes when some don't turn up in good faith.
explanation.definitionFit: The close of a story is its finish or conclusion.

clue.text: Get at aid organisation, being perturbed

indicators.note: organisation suggests putting the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Attacking a charity body leaves people upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone anxious and flustered.
